## The department

DIAD turns WOAH data into evidence and advice. It is organised in three business teams and one transversal team:

- **[The Observatory](observatory/index.qmd)** monitors the implementation of WOAH standards by Members.
- **[EPIQ](epiq/index.qmd)**, the EPIdemiology & Quantitative intelligence group, runs epidemic intelligence and risk analytics.
- **[Animal Health Econometrics](econometrics/index.qmd)** studies the economics of animal health.
- **[The Data Science Lab](dslab/index.qmd)** provides data products, pipelines, automation and AI to WOAH and its Members.

## DIAD in the WOAH data strategy

DIAD coordinates the execution of the data strategy, from collection to external sharing.

| Step | Where we are going |
|---|---|
| **Collect** | Increase the quality and coverage of officially reported data. Make automated online media monitoring and data scouting part of routine rapid risk assessment. |
| **Curate** | Complete the glossary, with DOIs. |
| **Analyse** | Publish situation reports openly. Leverage our network of collaborators to create value from WOAH data. |
| **Share internally** | Bring all technical datasets onto Fabric, with ownership kept by departments. |
| **Share externally** | Master datasets available through the API. MCP project for AI access. |

: {.woah-table}

These objectives contribute to three outcomes of WOAH's **8th Strategic Plan**: standards adaptable to all Members; decision-making to tackle global challenges; and leadership in animal health data.

## How this site works

- Each piece of technical material lives in its own public repository of the [DIA-Dpt-WOAH](https://github.com/orgs/DIA-Dpt-WOAH/) organisation.
- This site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and published on GitHub Pages.
- Reuse of WOAH data should cite WOAH as the source.
